turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I am waiting for Estella, and I grow impatient.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry, ma'am, I'll call her if you wish.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Hurry, boy, I have not all day to stand about.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Here, Estella, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Estella
turns.text: Mother, what is it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Play with this young man, Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I should, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Nonsense, boy, I command it.

turns.speaker: Estella
turns.text: Very well, I shall play with him.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, ma'am, but I'm afraid I must be going.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: No, no, you shall stay and play.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm so sorry, ma'am, but I really must go.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as you are told, boy.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I must insist, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Estella
turns.text: Mother, he seems reluctant.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence, Estella, I know what I am doing.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry if I've offended you, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You have not offended me, boy, you have simply disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll try to make it up to you, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: See that you do, boy.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
